title: Composition isomorphisms of etale inverse images of sheaves of sets, with units
statement: For a morphism of schemes $e:T\to S$ and a sheaf of sets $G$ on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets], $e^{-1}G$ denotes the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets: the sheafification of the presheaf $e_pG(V)=\varinjlim_{(U,\varphi)}G(U)$ on $T_{\Et}$, the colimit over the pairs of an object $U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and a $T$-morphism $\varphi:V\to U\times_ST$, i.e. $u_s$ for the functor $u:S_{\Et}\to T_{\Et}$, $U\mapsto U\times_ST$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] (1), of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (2) with values in sets (the construction of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] with values in sets); it is left adjoint to $e_*$, $(e_*H)(U)=H(U\times_ST)$. For an object $U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and $s\in G(U)$ write $e^*s\in(e^{-1}G)(U\times_ST)$ for the image of $s$ under the unit $G\to e_*e^{-1}G$. Let $f:Y\to X$ and $g:W\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Then for every sheaf of sets $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ there is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets $c_{f,g,F}:g^{-1}f^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ g)^{-1}F$ on $W_{\Et}$, natural in $F$, such that: (0) (units) for every morphism $e:T\to S$, every sheaf of sets $G$ on $S_{\Et}$, every morphism $a:U'\to U$ of $S_{\Et}$ and $s\in G(U)$, $e^*(s|_{U'})=(e^*s)|_{U'\times_ST}$, and for every morphism of sheaves $\psi:G\to G'$, $e^*(\psi_U(s))=(e^{-1}\psi)(e^*s)$; (1) $c_{f,g,F}(g^*(f^*s))=(f\circ g)^*s$ for every object $U$ of $X_{\Et}$ and every $s\in F(U)$, where $(U\times_XY)\times_YW$ is identified with $U\times_XW$ by the canonical isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]; and $c_{f,g,F}$ is the only morphism of sheaves $g^{-1}f^{-1}F\to(f\circ g)^{-1}F$ with this property; (2) (associativity) for a further morphism $h:V\to W$, the two isomorphisms $h^{-1}g^{-1}f^{-1}F\to(f\circ g\circ h)^{-1}F$, namely $c_{f\circ g,h,F}\circ h^{-1}(c_{f,g,F})$ and $c_{f,g\circ h,F}\circ c_{g,h,f^{-1}F}$, are equal.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites) and its proof ((u o v)_s = u_s o v_s), applied to the base change functors of small etale sites; used without statement in Etale Cohomology Lemma Tag 09ZF, proof, third paragraph ('compatible with pullback by morphisms in X_etale and by (finite) morphisms X' -> X in a manner which we leave to the reader to clarify'); the unit and associativity clauses are written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 1 (the unit on sections and clause (0)).* For $e:T\to S$, let $b_e:S_{\Et}\to T_{\Et}$ send $U$ to $U\times_ST$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] (1), $e^{-1}$ is the sheafification of the presheaf pullback along $b_e$ and is left adjoint to $e_*=(-)\circ b_e$ on sheaves of sets. The unit at $G$, evaluated on $U$, sends $s\in G(U)$ first to the coprojection of $s$ at $(U,\mathrm{id}_{U\times_ST})$ in $(e_pG)(U\times_ST)$ and then to its image under sheafification; this is $e^*s$. For $a:U'\to U$, naturality of the unit as a morphism of sheaves gives $e^*(G(a)(s))=(e^{-1}G)(b_ea)(e^*s)$, which is the first equation of (0). Naturality of the unit in $G$ gives $e_*(e^{-1}\psi)_U(e^*s)=e^*(\psi_U(s))$, the second equation of (0). The equalities also follow directly from the index morphisms $(U',\mathrm{id})\to(U,b_ea)$ in the presheaf colimits and functoriality of sheafification.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00VE (lemma-adjoints-u, unit at the identity-indexed coprojection), Lemma Tag 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves), and Lemma Tag 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites); the two naturality equations are written out here

proof.text: *Step 2 (direct images of a composite).* For an object $U\to X$, the two squares defining $(U\times_XY)\times_YW$ are cartesian, so their outer rectangle is cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the canonical $W$-isomorphism $\alpha_U:(U\times_XY)\times_YW\xrightarrow{\sim}U\times_XW$, compatible with both projections. For $a:U'\to U$, both composites from $(U'\times_XY)\times_YW$ to $U\times_XW$ obtained using $\alpha$ and base change of $a$ have the same two projections, so are equal. For a sheaf $H$ on $W_{\Et}$, applying the contravariant functor $H$ to $\alpha_U$ yields $d_{f,g,H}(U):((f\circ g)_*H)(U)=H(U\times_XW)\xrightarrow{\sim}H((U\times_XY)\times_YW)=(f_*g_*H)(U)$; projection compatibility gives compatibility with restrictions, and naturality of a sheaf morphism gives naturality in $H$. Thus $d_{f,g}:(f\circ g)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*g_*$ is an isomorphism of functors on sheaves of sets. For three arrows, the two ways of passing from a triple fibre product to $U\times_XV$ have the same projections to $U$ and $V$, and hence agree by the same universal property; therefore the corresponding $d$'s obey the associativity equation after applying any sheaf of sets.

source.place: Lemmas Tag 021I (lemma-morphism-big-small-etale) (2) and Tag 021J (lemma-composition-etale), proof; associativity of the canonical fibre-product comparison is written out here

proof.text: *Step 3 (the composition isomorphism and its unit equation).* Apply [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures] (1). It gives $L_1=g^{-1}f^{-1}\dashv R_1=f_*g_*$ with unit at $F$ equal to $f_*(\eta^g_{f^{-1}F})\circ\eta^f_F$. Put $L_2=(f\circ g)^{-1}\dashv R_2=(f\circ g)_*$ and use $d_{f,g}:R_2\xrightarrow{\sim}R_1$ from Step 2. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] there is a natural isomorphism $c_{f,g}:L_1\xrightarrow{\sim}L_2$, uniquely characterized among natural transformations by $R_1(c_{f,g,F})\circ f_*(\eta^g_{f^{-1}F})\circ\eta^f_F=d_{f,g,L_2F}\circ\eta^{f\circ g}_F$. At an etale object $U\to X$, the two sides send $s\in F(U)$, after identifying $(U\times_XY)\times_YW$ with $U\times_XW$ by $\alpha_U$, to $c_{f,g,F}(g^*(f^*s))$ and $(f\circ g)^*s$, respectively, by the unit description in Step 1. This proves the equality in (1), including naturality in $F$ and invertibility of $c_{f,g,F}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03CB (lemma-composition-morphisms-sites), proof: the two inverse images are left adjoints of the composite direct image; Definition Tag 03CC (definition-composition-morphisms-sites), sentence after it; unit equation by Categories Lemma Tag 0B65

proof.text: *Step 4 (uniqueness for a fixed $F$).* Let $q:g^{-1}f^{-1}F\to(f\circ g)^{-1}F$ be any sheaf morphism satisfying the equation of (1) for all $U,s$. Every section of $g^{-1}f^{-1}F$ on an object $V'\to W$ is locally the image under sheafification of a representative $(A,\varphi,t)$ with $A\to Y$ etale, $\varphi:V'\to A\times_YW$, and $t\in(f^{-1}F)(A)$: this is [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] applied to the defining presheaf colimit, whose elements have such representatives. Apply the same local-representation statement to $t$ for $f^{-1}F$: after pulling its covering of $A$ back along $V'\to A$, each restriction of $t$ is represented by $s\in F(U)$ and a morphism to $U\times_XY$. Thus, after the resulting covering of $V'$, the original section is a restriction of $g^*(f^*s)$ along a morphism into $(U\times_XY)\times_YW$. Both $q$ and $c_{f,g,F}$ send this section to the same restriction of $(f\circ g)^*s$ by (1); they commute with restrictions because they are sheaf morphisms. The sheaf condition makes their values equal on $V'$, for every section and every $V'$, hence $q=c_{f,g,F}$. This proves the objectwise uniqueness asserted in (1), which is stronger than uniqueness only among natural transformations.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), via Theorem Tag 00WB (theorem-plus), applied twice to the presheaf pullback in Lemma Tag 00WX; the fixed-object uniqueness omitted by Tag 03CB is written out here

proof.text: *Step 5 (associativity).* Let $f:X_1\to X_0$, $g:X_2\to X_1$, $h:X_3\to X_2$. Fix $F$ on $(X_0)_{\Et}$, $U\to X_0$ etale, and $s\in F(U)$. By Step 4, applied twice, sections of $h^{-1}g^{-1}f^{-1}F$ are locally restrictions of $h^*g^*f^*s$ (with varying $U,s$), so it suffices to compare the two morphisms in (2) on these sections. For the first composite, naturality of the unit $h^*$ in the sheaf morphism $c_{f,g,F}$ from Step 1 gives $h^{-1}(c_{f,g,F})(h^*g^*f^*s)=h^*(c_{f,g,F}(g^*f^*s))=h^*((f\circ g)^*s)$; Step 3 for $(f\circ g,h)$ sends this to $((f\circ g)\circ h)^*s$. For the second, Step 3 for $(g,h)$ sends $h^*g^*(f^*s)$ to $(g\circ h)^*(f^*s)$, and Step 3 for $(f,g\circ h)$ sends that to $(f\circ(g\circ h))^*s$. The two final sections agree under the canonical identification of the triple fibre products: their maps to $U$ and $X_3$ are identical, so the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies both with the pullback of $s$ along $f\circ g\circ h$ (the associativity of the $d$'s checked in Step 2). The two sheaf morphisms agree locally on every section and hence agree, proving (2). Empty covers and identity arrows cause no exception: the same unit equations and sheaf uniqueness apply.

split_report.summary: Split the sheaf-of-sets composition and unit statement into five steps following Stacks 03CB/03CC and the small-etale description 021I/021J. The unit is the identity-indexed coprojection followed by sheafification; fibre-product pasting gives the direct-image comparison; composite adjunction and uniqueness of left adjoints give the isomorphism; the local-section description of sheafification proves uniqueness for each fixed sheaf, and that uniqueness plus the unit formulas gives associativity. No new DAG nodes were needed; the cited Lean composition and coherence declarations have abelian coefficients and do not state this sets claim.
